Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the performance looked promising. Procurement asked me to pull together a tighter ask so we can evaluate next steps. We’re specifically interested in the Optimize toolkit (batching/caching guidance + quantization recommendations) and how that maps to commercial concessions for a 6–12 month pilot.

High-level:
- Production workload: customer-facing summarization + retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) for healthcare docs.
- Average sequence lengths: prompt ~120 tokens, completion ~220 tokens.
- Monthly usage estimate: ~85M generated tokens (initial), expected to grow to ~200M if pilot succeeds.

Questions:
1) Can you share a simple savings model we can use to project token-unit cost reductions from batching + prefix caching vs. enabling 8-bit quantization? We need something procurement can put into a spreadsheet.
2) What accuracy guardrails do you recommend for quantization on open models — thresholds we can ask our ML team to validate?
3) For a pilot, what credit structure and discount cadence do you normally offer (e.g., pilot credits + early-stage committed discount vs. volume-based tiering)?

If useful, I can share a sample trace for a few calls. Also, we’d like an itemized attachment we can circulate internally (procurement + ML infra).

Appreciate any templates or examples.

Best,

Ava — great to hear from you and glad the demo resonated. Attached is a compact pilot one-pager and a starter cost-model workbook I put together for similar RAG workloads. Quick notes up front:

- Typical savings mix: batching (throughput uplift) yields ~15–30% effective token-cost reduction for conversational back-and-forth patterns; prefix/KV caching yields up to 40% savings on workloads with repeated context (search-results + templated prompts); quantization (8-bit) can reduce GPU runtime cost by ~20–50% depending on hardware and kernel availability. The workbook models conservative/likely/aggressive scenarios.
- Accuracy guardrails: as a sales rule-of-thumb we recommend a max 5% relative drop on a task-specific metric (e.g., ROUGE or top-1 accuracy) before reverting or running selective higher-precision inference. We can help produce a small eval harness for your test prompts.
- Pilot commercial structure we suggest: 3-month pilot with: 1) $X in usage credits (we typically cover ~30–50% of expected pilot consumption up to an agreed cap), 2) a technical onboarding package (Redwood Solutions time), and 3) a path to a 12-month committed band with stepped discounts if you hit thresholds. We’ll customize depending on whether you need Hosted vs Dedicated.

I’ve attached:
- peregrine_pilot_onepager.pdf (pilot scope, success criteria, timelines)
- cost_model_peregrine.xlsx (editable — conservative/likely/aggressive tabs)

Next steps: if you can drop a short sample (10–20) of real requests (anonymized) and confirm whether you expect repeated prefix patterns (e.g., patient history blocks being reused), Marissa and Connor will propose a pilot credit amount and a lightweight technical validation plan.

Available for a call tomorrow afternoon PT if that helps.

Cheers,

Hi Ava — looping in Connor (solutions) + adding technical detail. Short version up front: we can run a quantified validation suite on your redacted prompts and target metrics, and gate quantization activation behind a per-prompt confidence threshold and regression alerts. More detail: 

Technical validation plan (3 parts):
1) Local eval harness: we run your provided sample batch against baseline FP16 and an 8-bit quantized variant on a mirrored infra to measure relative deltas on metrics you pick (ROUGE, BLEU, retrieval F1, clinician-rated correctness). We deliver a report with example failure modes.
2) Canary rollout: enable quantized serving for 5–10% of traffic behind logging + A/B quality checks; automatic rollback if metric breaches (we recommend 3 consecutive days above a 5% relative drop).
3) Telemetry + traces: during pilot we expose per-route token-cost, 95th/99th latency, cache hit-rate, batching efficiency (tokens-per-batch), and a quantization-fail rate metric. All surfaced in Redwood Console and via a daily/weekly export to your secure S3/GDrive.

Commercial pilot options we typically propose for clinical-regulated customers:
- Option A (Conservative): 3-month pilot, Redwood provides 40% of expected pilot consumption as credits, quantization is locally validated but disabled in production unless approved.
- Option B (Accelerated): 3-month pilot, Redwood provides 60% credits plus a 6-week canary with quant enabled for low-risk routes; if metrics hold, we extend to production with a 6–12 month commit discount (tiered).

On Hosted vs Dedicated: hosted gives fastest time-to-value with our managed quant kernels on supported hardware; Dedicated provides more control (you can accept some additional variance for cheaper instance types), but requires an onboarding window to ensure quant kernels/compilers are validated for your stack. We’ll scope that in the SOW if you choose Dedicated.

Connor, can you add an example credit cadence we could propose?

Thanks,
Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
